newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares recover to end barely lower.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares recover to end barely lower.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended little changed in range-bound and quiet trade on Tuesday as the index rebounded on support near the index's 1,600 level, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed down three points, or 0.18 percent at 1,644 after brushing a low of 1,621. On Monday, it lost 1.32 percent in correction of last week's 4.6 percent jump.
Daily trade volume shrank to 14.78 trillion lira from Monday's 18.48 trillion.

"The index has strong support at 1,600. Technically, direction is up, but selective activity has not spilled over to the whole market because of ongoing political uncertainty," said Deniz Yurtseven from Ekinciler securities.
"If uncertainty fades, the market may rally towards 2,000 level this month," he added.
The index's all-time high close was 1,700 on January 27. The 1997 intra-day high was 1,751 in January.
Brokers said the market continued to watch political developments but with less anxiety than in previous weeks.
BBP, a key far-right party said on Monday it would not join a caretaker government sought by the ailing Islamist-led coalition, jeopardising the alliance's plans for early elections.

The government, which has a thin majority in parliament relies on the BBP's support to get the necessary parliamentary approval for snap elections planned to be held by end-1997. A majority vote is needed to set a date for the polls.

Analysts say the junior coalition party's conservative deputies displeased with the failure of their Islamist partners to meet army-led demands for a crackdown on religious activism may vote against early polls.
The main opposition Motherland Party also plans another censure motion against the 11-month-old Islamist-led coalition.

Of the 243 shares traded, 89 declined, 77 advanced and 77 were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial eased 0.46 percent to 1,527, the IMKB Services shed 0.3 percent to 1,638 while the IMKB Financial firmed 0.33 percent to 1,810.

Leading actives were utilities Kepez Elektrik, down 5,000 lira at 280,000, Cukurova Elektrik, down 2,500 lira at 222,500 and largely state owned oil refiner Tupras, up 3,000 lira at 81,000. They made up 18.9 percent of the total turnover.
